collekt ships a **source-adapter** for each supported provider. An adapter knows
how to fetch source-native files for a request and how to plan (dry-run) the same
work. Adapters are registered on import (`collekt.sources`) and selected by a
source's `kind`.

## Built-in adapters

| Kind | Produces | Access | Format |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cmems` | Gridded ocean fields (currents, SST, waves, biogeochemistry) | open | NetCDF |
| `ecmwf_open_data` | Gridded forecast wind | open | GRIB2 |
| `era5` | Gridded reanalysis wind | credentials (CDS) | NetCDF |
| `copernicus_dataspace` | Sentinel / Landsat product files | credentials | product (e.g. `.zip`) |
| `skytruth` | Oil-slick detections (features) | open | Parquet |
| `hozint` | Threat-intelligence reports (features) | credentials | Parquet |
| `eodyn` | eOdyn surface currents / drifters | credentials | NetCDF |

Open sources need no secrets; credential-gated sources resolve their secrets from
the environment or provider tools — see [Credentials](credentials.qmd). The eOdyn
adapter serves a historical preview archive (`mode: archive`) until the
production API ships (`mode: api`).

## Bundled catalog

collekt ships a **curated catalog** of concrete datasets — the datasets AI4COPSEC
uses, grouped into catalogs under `collekt/conf/source/`:

| Catalog | Sources |
|---|---|
| `cmems_global` | `cmems_glorys_nrt`, `cmems_glorys_my`, `cmems_duacs_nrt`, `cmems_duacs_my`, `cmems_global_sst_nrt`, `cmems_global_sst_my`, `cmems_global_waves`, `cmems_global_chl_obs_nrt`, `cmems_global_chl_obs_my`, `cmems_global_bgc_model` |
| `cmems_med` | `cmems_med_currents_nrt`, `cmems_med_currents_nrt_15min`, `cmems_med_currents_nrt_2d_hourly`, `cmems_med_currents_nrt_3d_hourly`, `cmems_med_currents_my`, `cmems_med_waves`, `cmems_med_chl_obs`, `cmems_med_bgc_model` |
| `cmems_ibi` | `cmems_ibi_currents`, `cmems_ibi_waves`, `cmems_atl_chl_obs_nrt`, `cmems_atl_chl_obs_my`, `cmems_ibi_bgc_model` |
| `cmems_nws` | `cmems_nws_currents`, `cmems_nws_waves`, `cmems_nws_chl_obs`, `cmems_nws_bgc_model` |
| `ecmwf` | `ecmwf_open_data_forecast`, `era5_reanalysis` |
| `eodyn` | `eodyn_osmose_currents` |
| `skytruth` | `skytruth` |
| `dataspace` | `copernicus_s1_grd`, `copernicus_s2_l2a`, `copernicus_landsat` |

Select concrete sources by name and select variables from each source's
`available_variables` allow-list:

```bash
collekt config show                                    # inspect the catalog
collekt fetch --bbox -6 20 35 45 --start 2023-06-15 \
  --datasource cmems_duacs_my --use-variables cmems_duacs_my=ugos,vgos
```

The catalog is **curated, not exhaustive** — dataset IDs drift, so
`collekt doctor --online` validates the CMEMS entries against the provider
catalogue.

Each gridded source declares one temporal field: `temporal_sampling`, the
native cadence of that dataset (`15min`, `1h`, `3h`, `6h`, or `24h`). A request's
`--sampling` can be that cadence or a coarser integer multiple of it; for example,
a `15min` dataset can be downloaded at `15min`, `1h`, `3h`, `6h`, or `24h`, but a
daily dataset can only satisfy `24h` requests. When a provider offers multiple
cadences or dimensionalities, model them as separate source entries (for example
`cmems_med_currents_nrt_15min`, `cmems_med_currents_nrt_2d_hourly`, and
`cmems_med_currents_nrt`) so each source maps to one provider dataset and one
actual cadence.

Regional Atlantic products use the CMEMS regional names: IBI (`cmems_ibi`) and
European North-West Shelf (`cmems_nws`) are separate catalogs. Basin-level
Atlantic ocean-colour observations keep `cmems_atl` in their source names.

Sources may also declare a `coverage` block:

```yaml
coverage:
  longitude: [-19.08, 5.08]
  latitude: [26.17, 56.08]
  temporal:
    start: "2022-11-23"
    end: null
    kind: rolling
```

This is an offline planning hint. Static spatial bounds and stable temporal
starts are shipped in the catalog; rolling/NRT products keep `end: null` because
their latest date moves. When online catalogue access is available, CMEMS
planning still prefers Copernicus Marine `describe()` and `collekt doctor
--online` compares declared coverage with the provider catalogue.

## Extending and overriding

Downstream is expected to select a subset and add its own sources. Two ways:

- **Python** — `get_config(overrides=...)` deep-merges on top of the catalog:

  ```python
  cfg = get_config(overrides={"sources": {
      "cmems_duacs_my": {"use_variables": ["ugos", "vgos"]},
      "my_source": {
          "kind": "cmems",
          "dataset_id": "...",
          "available_variables": ["thetao"],
          "use_variables": ["thetao"],
          "temporal_sampling": "24h",
      },
  }})
  ```

- **A `conf_dir` overlay** — a `default.yaml` whose `source_catalogs` can name the
  **bundled** catalogs (resolved automatically) alongside its own `source/*.yaml`,
  and whose `sources:` block adds or overrides individual sources.

Curated **presets** and **variable-group tagging** are deliberately left to
downstream — they are use-case decisions, not universal ones. Bundled sources
carry no `variable_groups`, so an untagged source is treated as a wildcard
(selected by name, never excluded by a request's `--variables`); tag your own
sources downstream if you want group-based selection.

## Dependencies

collekt installs all provider clients and the gridded `Assembler` by default, so
every source works out of the box after `uv sync`. Clients are imported lazily,
so importing collekt stays fast and a source only pulls its client into memory
when it actually runs. The ECMWF Open Data forecast subset and Skytruth need no
credentials; the other providers do — see [Credentials](credentials.qmd).
